tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

delaySeconds.description: Seconds from now to wake up. Clamped to [60, 3600] by the runtime. Required unless `stop` is true.

reason.description: One short sentence explaining the chosen delay. Goes to telemetry and is shown to the user. Be specific. Required unless `stop` is true.

prompt.description: The /loop input to fire on wake-up. Pass the same /loop input verbatim each turn so the next firing re-enters the skill and continues the loop. For autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` instead (the dynamic-pacing variant, not the CronCreate-mode `<<autonomous-loop>>`). Required unless `stop` is true.

stop.description: Set to true to end the dynamic loop immediately instead of scheduling another wakeup. When true, all other fields are ignored and no further wakeups fire.

noop.description: true = nothing changed (you checked and there is nothing to report). false = something happened worth keeping (edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, surfaced a finding). Consecutive noop:true ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak. Required unless `stop` is true.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

skill.description: The name of a skill from the available-skills list. Do not guess names.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

query.description: Query to find deferred tools. Use "select:<tool_name>" for direct selection, or keywords to search.

max_results.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

tools.name: Workflow
tools.description:
Execute a workflow script that orchestrates multiple subagents deterministically. Workflows run in the background — this tool returns immediately with a task ID, and a <task-notification> arrives when the workflow completes. Use /workflows to watch live progress.

ONLY call this tool when the user has explicitly opted into multi-agent orchestration. Workflows can spawn dozens of agents and consume a large amount of tokens; the user must request that scale, not have it inferred. Explicit opt-in means one of:
- The user included the keyword "ultracode" in their prompt (you'll see a system-reminder confirming it).
- Ultracode is on for the session (a system-reminder confirms it) — see **Ultracode** in the workflow authoring reference.
- The user directly asked you to run a workflow or use multi-agent orchestration in their own words ("use a workflow", "run a workflow", "fan out agents", "orchestrate this with subagents"). The ask must be in the user's words — a task that would merely benefit from a workflow does not count.
- The user invoked a skill or slash command whose instructions tell you to call Workflow.
- The user asked you to run a specific named or saved workflow.

For any other task — even one that would clearly benefit from parallelism — do NOT call this tool. Use the Agent tool (if available) for individual subagents, or briefly describe what a multi-agent workflow could do and how much it would roughly cost, and ask the user whether to run it. Mention they can ask for one with "use a workflow" in a future message to skip the ask.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`: a PURE LITERAL (no variables, calls or interpolation) giving the workflow's `name`, a one-line `description` (shown in the permission dialog) and optionally `phases` — one `{ title, detail? }` per phase() call, titles matched exactly. Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first, and do not also set the tool's `name` input (that selects a saved workflow); it is plain JavaScript, not TypeScript.

The canonical multi-stage pattern — pipeline by default, each dimension verifies as soon as its review completes:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'review-changes',
    description: 'Review changed files across dimensions, verify each finding',
    phases: [{ title: 'Review' }, { title: 'Verify' }],
  }
  const DIMENSIONS = [{key: 'bugs', prompt: '...'}, {key: 'perf', prompt: '...'}]
  const results = await pipeline(
    DIMENSIONS,
    d => agent(d.prompt, {label: `review:${d.key}`, phase: 'Review', schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA}),
    review => parallel(review.findings.map(f => () =>
      agent(`Adversarially verify: ${f.title}`, {label: `verify:${f.file}`, phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})
        .then(v => ({...f, verdict: v}))
    ))
  )
  const confirmed = results.flat().filter(Boolean).filter(f => f.verdict?.isReal)
  return { confirmed }
  // Dimension 'bugs' findings verify while dimension 'perf' is still reviewing. No wasted wall-clock.

Before writing a script, load the `workflow-authoring` skill — the workflow authoring reference: script API and gotchas, resume, the **Ultracode** section, quality patterns, worked examples.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

input.question: In the Nosto search facet manager, after facets are created, can (1) the order of facets be changed, and (2) the order of values within a terms facet (e.g. sizes XS, S, M, L) be set manually or with a custom sort? Can facet values be grouped or merged (e.g. "XS (0-2)" covering XS, 0 and 2)?
input.goal: Replicate Shopify Search & Discovery filters (manually ordered and grouped Size values, facet order Product type, Price, Color, Size) in a Nosto Search Templates implementation for a Shopify store.

content.text:
**In Search Templates, you can control the displayed order in the frontend.** The docs don’t confirm controls in the facet manager for manually ordering facets or terms-facet values.

* **Facet order:** Render the facets in an explicit sequence, such as Product type, Price, Color, Size. The Search API returns facets, and the template controls how they’re displayed.
* **Value order:** Sort the terms facet’s `data` before rendering it. That lets you display sizes as XS, S, M, L regardless of the returned order.
* **Grouped values:** You can show a custom label such as “XS (0–2)” in the template, but this is a presentation-level mapping, not a merged facet value. To make it filter products tagged `XS`, `0`, or `2`, apply those underlying values as filters on the same field. The API joins multiple values for one field with OR. Counts for a combined option would also need custom handling.

The [Implementing Search page](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-code-editor/implementing-search-page) shows rendering `facet.data` and using `toggleProductFilter`; the [Implement Search results page](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-api/implementing-search-page) documents facet values and same-field filter behavior.

content.text:
Yes, there is one: the `nosto-docs` server. It searches Nosto's developer docs, so it can't see what the Admin screens actually offer. I asked it, and checked the search API's own facet settings type (`InputSearchFacetConfig` in `@nosto/nosto-js`) as well:

| Question | Answer | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Can the order of facets be changed? | **Yes.** Each facet has a `position` setting. The template can also override it from code by facet ID, with `customFacets` | API type, Nosto FAQ |
| Can the order of values be set by hand (XS, S, M, L)? | **No.** A terms facet's `order` is only `"count"` or by name, so there's no manual order | API type |
| Can values be grouped ("XS (0-2)")? | **No native support.** The docs say to do it in the template: show the group label, and apply XS, 0 and 2 as filters on the same field, which Nosto combines with OR. Counts for a group need custom handling | `askQuestion` answer |

Neither answer confirms what the Admin facet manager shows on screen. The docs don't describe it, and the `position` setting suggests facet order can be changed there, but no one has checked.

**What this means:**
- **Facet order** (Product type, Price, Color, Size) can be set without template code. Someone checks the Admin facet manager first; if it isn't there, I set `position` in code.
- **Size order** can't be set by hand in Nosto. Asking the Tahari team won't get them the Search & Discovery-style control.
- **Grouping** can only happen in our template. That's option A from before.

So Size order and grouping become one template job: a size map with each group label, its raw values, and their order, copied from the Search & Discovery setup. Whoever owns that setup gives us the membership; after that, changes are an edit to the map.

Do you want me to go with that? If so, I need the group membership: which raw sizes each Search & Discovery group covers, including where XXS goes.

content.text:
Every search goes through `withBaseConfig` in `src/config.ts:71`, so either option is a small change there or in the filter drawer. There are two ways to do it.

**1. Ask Nosto to return them in order** (the documented method). Set `position` for each facet ID in the request:

```ts
// src/config.ts — withBaseConfig
products: {
  ...
  customFacets: [
    { id: "6ada5f5a573df0b66199a0f0", position: 0 }, // Product type
    { id: "6ada7dfc573df0b66100bac2", position: 1 }, // Price
    { id: "6ada6140573df0b6619a7860", position: 2 }, // Color
    { id: "6ada5fb7fb1b02ffcbcceb04", position: 3 }  // Size
  ]
}
```

- **Upside:** this is Nosto's own documented override.
- **Downside:** the code hard-codes this account's facet IDs. If someone deletes and recreates a facet in the Admin, its ID changes and that facet silently falls out of order.

**2. Sort them in our filter drawer by field.** Nosto keeps returning the Admin order, and the drawer renders them in a fixed order:

```ts
// Live's order (Search & Discovery); facets not listed keep Nosto's order after these
const facetOrder = ["productType", "skus.price", "skus.customFields.color", "skus.customFields.size"]
```

- **Upside:** it uses field names, which don't change if a facet is recreated. A new facet someone adds in the Admin still shows up, after the listed ones.
- **Downside:** to change the order, someone has to change our code. A field name only changes if the facet is pointed at a different field, as Color might be for issue 3.

I'd recommend option 2. It's less fragile, and the Size value order and grouping map will live in the same filter code, so everything that copies Search & Discovery sits in one place.

Should I go ahead with option 2? It's a small change, and I'd check it on your dev theme with the `nosto:dev` build running.

/** Returned facet position in search response facets array */
position?: number;
```

The FAQ links to the same type in Nosto's GraphQL schema (https://search.nosto.com/v1/graphql?ref=InputSearchFacetConfig).

input.question: For a Shopify store using the Nosto Shopify app, can product metafields (including Shopify category metafields such as shopify.color-pattern, which are lists of metaobject references) be indexed into the Nosto catalog as custom fields so they can be used as search facets? How are customFields populated for Shopify products and SKUs?
input.goal: Replace a Nosto Color facet built from raw variant colour names with Shopify's taxonomy base colours (Black, Blue, Beige...) to match Shopify Search & Discovery filters, and show colour swatches.

content.text:
**Yes, metafield-derived values can be used as Nosto custom fields, but the docs do not confirm that the Nosto Shopify app automatically imports Shopify metafields or category metafields.** For `shopify.color-pattern`, confirm its app-sync behavior separately; the documented approach is to map the desired value into Nosto’s product data.

* **Product-level fields:** Send values under `custom_fields` on the product. Product tagging also supports custom fields as key–value pairs, such as `color_taxonomy: "Black"`. See [Default Product Tagging](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-on-your-website/manual-implementation/product-tagging/default-product-tagging) and the [Updating Products](/techdocs/apis/rest/products/updating-products-using-the-products-api).
* **SKU-level fields:** Put variant-specific values under each SKU’s own `custom_fields`, such as `color: "Blue"`. See [Extending tagging with SKUs](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-on-your-website/advanced-implementation/extending-tagging-with-skus).
* **Facets:** Configure a facet for the custom field in Nosto. Search refers to it as `customFields.color_taxonomy`; see [Implement Search results page](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-api/implementing-search-page).

For your color facet, map Shopify’s taxonomy value to a normalized field such as `color_taxonomy: "Black"` and facet that field. The docs don’t specify how Shopify list-of-metaobject-reference values are converted, so don’t assume Nosto will resolve them into color names automatically.

input.question: Is there a setting in the Nosto admin (facet manager or search settings) to hide or turn off facet value counts, for Search Templates or the Search API?
input.goal: Hide the (n) product counts next to filter values so the filter drawer matches a Shopify theme that doesn't show counts.

content.text:
**No facet-manager or Search settings toggle is documented for hiding facet counts.** Counts are returned as `data.count` for terms facets, and the Search Templates example displays them explicitly in its UI.

* **Search Templates:** Remove the `({value.count})` output from your facet component. The [Implementing Search page](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-code-editor/implementing-search-page) shows where it is rendered.
* **Search API:** You control which response fields you request. Omit `count` from the GraphQL selection, or keep requesting it and simply don’t display it. See [Implement Search results page](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-api/implementing-search-page).

This changes the presentation, not the facet filtering behavior.

content.text:
The `COLOR_` tags are in Nosto's index, so we can build a Color facet on them.

**Coverage for "dress"** (85 Nosto results):
- **Tagged:** 65 products have exactly one `COLOR_` tag.
- **Untagged:** 20 have none, for example Mila Milano Sculpt Dress, Savannah Lace-Trim Satin Jacquard Dress and Raven Keyhole Midi Dress. A colour filter on tags would never show them.
- **Values:** `COLOR_Black` 25, `Blue` 10, `Red` 7, `Brown` 7, `White` 6, `Purple` 3, `Pink` 2, `Beige` 2, `Yellow` 1, `Green` 1, `COLOR_MULTI` 1. Apart from `MULTI` (Shopify calls it "Multicolor"), these are the same names as live's Shopify colours.

**What the facet needs** (Nosto Admin → Facet manager → Create):

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Name | `Color` |
| Product attribute | product **Tags** (the API field `tags1`). This is product-level, not the current "SKU custom field: color" |
| Facet type | Select |
| Sorting method | Alphabetic |
| Prefix | `COLOR_`, so only the colour tags come back and not the other ~20 tags per product |
| Existing Color facet | switch it off, or point it at Tags |

**Prefix in the Admin:** I don't know whether the Admin has a prefix option. The API supports one (`prefix` in the facet settings), so if the Admin doesn't, I'd set `prefix: ["COLOR_"]` from our code, which needs the new facet's ID. Like `position`, I haven't tested it.

**Template work** (ours, after the facet exists):
- **Labels:** strip `COLOR_` from the label, and show `MULTI` as "Multicolor".
- **Swatches:** use live's markup: `swatch__button` with the theme's square or circle style, a `background-color`, and the grey empty state for Multicolor.
- **Colours:** the hex values come from Shopify's taxonomy colours I captured from live (Black `#000000`, Blue `#005BD3`, Navy `#282099`…). I'd have the theme output them, not hard-code them. Whether Liquid can read them on the search page still needs checking.

**Decision needed:** whether 20 of 85 dresses having no colour tag is acceptable. Either the Elie Tahari team tags them, or those products don't appear under any colour. I don't yet know whether those 20 have a category colour on live, so live may be filtering them correctly today. I'll check that next if you want.

The screenshot shows the same mechanism as the search page. I checked live's `/collections/dresses` and the Color filter there is the same Shopify filter:

- **The filter:** `filter.v.t.shopify.color-pattern`, Shopify's category colour on the product, filtered through Search & Discovery.
- **The rendering:** Broadcast's `snippets/filters.liquid:157-200` outputs each value's `filter_value.swatch.color` as `<div class="swatch__button swatch__button--square" style="background-color: #EAD8AB;">`. Multicolor has no colour, so it gets the `swatch__button--empty` grey with a dashed border, as in your screenshot.
- **The colours:** Shopify supplies the hex values from its standard taxonomy colours (Beige `#EAD8AB`, Black `#000000`, Blue `#005BD3`, Bronze `#CD7F32`…). Broadcast doesn't define them.

So yes, that's the only mechanism. Native Broadcast uses no tags and no theme colour settings; it's all Shopify filter data. I didn't mean that live uses tags. The `COLOR_` tags were a possible way to get the same base colour into Nosto, since Nosto won't pull the category colour.

**On "they haven't been tagging":** the tags are there. 65 of 85 dresses have one (`COLOR_Black`, `COLOR_Red`…), alongside other tags in the same style like `LENGTH_Midi` and `CATEGORIES_Dresses`. That looks like an import or integration adding them rather than someone tagging by hand. That's my guess, not something I've checked. If no one on the Tahari team maintains them, that explains why 20 have none, and it's a reason not to rely on them without asking.

So the options for matching your screenshot in Nosto are:
1. **Use the `COLOR_` tags.** They're closest to live's values, but 20 of 85 products have none, and we don't know who keeps them up to date.
2. **Ask Nosto to index the category colour some other way.** For example, a regular product metafield that a Shopify Flow copies from the category colour. Nosto said they don't pull the *category* metafield; I don't know whether they pull custom ones.
3. **Ask the Tahari team where the `COLOR_` tags come from** before choosing.

For either 1 or 2, the swatch markup and hex values would copy Broadcast's exactly, as in your screenshot.

content.text:
All of this is in `snippets/filters.liquid`, in the theme repo (`~/Documents/roswell-studios/Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_2026`). The file is the same on `main` and on our branch, and unchanged since the initial blank Broadcast theme commit, so it's stock Broadcast.

- `snippets/filters.liquid:157`: `{%- if filter.presentation == 'swatch' -%}`. This is where the filter's "swatch" presentation setting from Search & Discovery switches the swatch on.
- `snippets/filters.liquid:167`: `{%- if filter_value.swatch.image != blank -%}`. This renders an image swatch when the value has one.
- `snippets/filters.liquid:191`: `style="background-color: {{ filter_value.swatch.color }};"`. This is the solid colour swatch, and the hex comes from Shopify.
- `snippets/filters.liquid:195`: adds `swatch__button--empty` when the value has no colour and no image, which gives Multicolor its dashed grey box.

The square shape comes from the `swatch_button_style` capture at the top of the same file (`snippets/filters.liquid:5-10`), based on `settings.swatch_style`.

content.text:
Your test value comes back in the response, and our request already asks for it: ```json { "value": "Amethyst", "count": 1, "selected": true, "visual": { "type": "color", "value": "#A54DCF" } } { "value": "Arabesque Print", "count": 1, "selected": false, "visual": null } ``` - **What the request asks for:** the search library already requests `visual { type value }` on every facet value, so nothing on the request side needs to change. - **What `visual` can be:** per the API type (`SearchFacetValueVisual`, `nosto.d.ts:3157`), `type` is `"color"` or `"thumbnail"`, matching the Admin's Color and Image choices. `"None"` gives `visual: null`. - **What we do with it now:** nothing. Our `TermsFacet.tsx` ignores `visual` and still uses BaubleBar's `var(--{handle})` CSS variable, which Elie Tahari doesn't define. So swatches can be set in Nosto Admin, and the template code to draw them in Broadcast's markup is straightforward: | Nosto `visual` | Renders as (`filters.liquid` equivalent) | |---|---| | `{type: "color"}` | `
` (line 191) | | `{type: "thumbnail"}` | `swatch__button` holding an `` (line 167) | | `null` | `swatch__button swatch__button--empty`, the grey dashed box (line 195) | The square or circle class comes from the theme's `swatch_style`, which the theme would pass to us as a data attribute. **There's also "Merge facet values" at the top right of your screenshot.** If it does what the name says, it may solve both problems in the Admin: - **Size:** merge XS, 0 and 2 into one value named "XS (0-2)", copying the Search & Discovery groups. - **Color:** merge Amethyst, Grape and Purple Haze into "Purple" with one swatch. That would turn the 40+ variant names into live's base colours, with no tags and no Shopify category data. I don't know from the docs how merged values appear in the response, or whether filtering on a merged value matches all the original values. Could you merge two Size values as a test, for example XS and 0 into "XS (0-2)"? I'll check the response and confirm that filtering on it returns products from both. Should I build the swatch rendering from `visual` now? It's a change to `TermsFacet.tsx` plus one data attribute in the theme. It doesn't depend on how merging turns out.

content.text: Filter swatches now come from the colour or image you set on each facet value in Nosto Admin. On your dev theme they render exactly like live's. **Checked against live on the same row:** | | Live | Ours | |---|---|---| | Swatch size | 16 × 16px | 16 × 16px | | Swatch offset in label | 22.25px | 22.25px | | Gap to text | 8px | 8px | | Row height | 17.1px | 17.1px | | Markup | `.shopify-swatch > .swatch__button.swatch__button--square` | same | - **Your Amethyst test** shows its `#A54DCF` swatch. - **Values with no colour or image** show the theme's grey dashed empty box, which is what live does for Multicolor. **How it works:** - **New component:** `src/shared/filters/FilterSwatch.tsx` reproduces `filters.liquid:157-200`. A Color visual becomes a `background-color` (with `data-swatch="white"` for `#FFFFFF`, as the theme does). An Image visual becomes an ``. None becomes the empty box. - **Which facets get swatches:** Nosto has no per-facet "swatch" option like Search & Discovery's, so a facet shows swatches as soon as any of its values has a visual. Size and Product type have none, so they stay plain. - **Theme settings respected:** "Enable swatches" and square/circle (`enable_swatches`, `swatch_style`) now reach the template as data attributes. With swatches off, none render. - **Removed:** BaubleBar's `var(--colour-name)` swatch. **Not tested in the browser:** the Image option and the circle style, because nothing uses either yet. Unit tests cover both. Typecheck and lint pass, and all 206 unit tests pass. content.thinking: Nosto already indexes Elie Tahari's category colour via the `shopify-color-pattern` field, but stores it as unresolved metaobject IDs rather than readable names like "Black." I'll check how many products have this field and whether any list multiple colours.

content.text:
Nosto does index Elie Tahari's category colour, but in a form that's hard to use as a filter directly.

**What's in Nosto for "dress"** (85 products):
- **Coverage:** 62 products have `shopify-color-pattern`. The `COLOR_` tags covered 65, and the two groups only partly overlap.
- **Values are IDs:** each value is a Shopify metaobject ID, not a colour name. These metaobjects are the store's own colour entries, each linked to a base colour, so several IDs share one base colour. For example, `181671461001`, `173077004425`, `172347752585` and `249252970633` are all on products tagged `COLOR_Blue`.
- **Multi-colour products:** 18 products list more than one colour, and Nosto treats the whole list as one value (`["gid://…/178375950473","gid://…/173998538889"]`). So a facet on this field gives 32 values, mostly combinations, rather than one value per colour. Nosto doesn't split the lists. BaubleBar's facets show the same thing (`["Beaded","Statement"]`).

**How BaubleBar avoids this:** its `filters.color` is a plain list of text, `["Blue"]`, so values are already readable names. Most of its products have one colour, so combinations are rare.

**What that means for Elie Tahari's Color facet:**

| Source | Readable names | One value per colour | Coverage (dress) | Setup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `skus.customFields.color` (current) | yes, variant names | yes | all | merge into base colours in Admin and set visuals, or set a visual per name |
| `shopify-color-pattern` | no, IDs | **no**, combinations | 62/85 | rename and merge each ID in Admin; combinations still broken |
| `COLOR_` tags | yes | yes | 65/85 | facet on tags with prefix; who maintains the tags is unknown |
| New text metafield, BaubleBar-style (e.g. a Flow copying the base colour name into `custom.color_family` as text) | yes | depends on how it's written | whatever the Flow covers | Shopify Flow plus a Nosto re-sync |

So BaubleBar's approach would work here, but only with a new metafield the Tahari team creates and fills; Elie Tahari has nothing like it today. Of what exists now, the current variant colour facet merged into base colours in the Admin is the most complete, since every product has a variant colour. The catch is that every new seasonal colour name has to be added to a merge.

I'd recommend asking Nosto whether they can resolve `shopify-color-pattern` to the base colour name and index each colour separately. That would give exactly what Shopify's filter uses, with no maintenance. Until then, merge the variant colours.

```

- **Field:** a product field, `customFields.shopify-color-pattern`, the same name the facet manager would use. Nosto names indexed metafields `namespace-key`, so Shopify's `shopify.color-pattern` becomes `shopify-color-pattern`. It isn't per variant: it sits on the product, not under `skus.customFields` like `color` and `size`.
- **Value:** one **string** holding a JSON-encoded list of Shopify metaobject IDs, exactly as Shopify stores a list-of-references metafield. Nosto doesn't follow the references, so the colour's name ("Black"), its linked base colour and its swatch hex aren't in the index.
- **Other category metafields:** they're stored the same way, for example `shopify-size`, `shopify-fabric`, `shopify-neckline` and `shopify-dress-style`.

**How a facet on it would split values — not tested.** I said a facet on this field would treat each list as one value. That isn't tested on this field. I inferred it from the value being a single string, and from BaubleBar's live facets returning lists as single values (`["Beaded","Statement"]`). To confirm, create a facet on `shopify-color-pattern` in the facet manager. You don't need to enable it on the site; check its preview for whether a two-colour product shows up as one combined value or under both IDs.

content.text:
Title: Product images
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/template-customization/product-images
Content: If you update a new image version for an old product, preferably save the image with a new file name, which typically generates a new image url for the product image as well.

Nosto doesn’t recognize images by file size or image content but by URL, hence if a url for an image is unaltered, Nosto doesn’t update image version in it’s index and uses older version of the product image in recommendations. On the contrary, new products and product images are automatically fetched and processed and no manual input is needed.

Manual re-index for an image version can be launched by enabling debug-mode and clicking Send Product Update Request-button on a product page.

For a full re-index, log in to Nosto’s admin and navigate to Tools > Products > Update products.

Title: Using Search Templates
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-code-editor/using-the-code-editor
Content: Project structure has the following requirements:

index.js - this is application entry point that is used when building project. When building project it will recursively scan this file for imports.
build/ - this directory stores build output that will be used when deploying project.

Title: Dynamic product cards
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/using-search-templates-starter/customizations/dynamic-product-cards
Content: When using dynamic product cards, the HTML for the cards is fetched directly from the merchant's website. This means that the styling for these cards is not included in the starter template's CSS.

To visually test the dynamic product cards in your local development environment, you need to include your store's CSS. You can do this by adding a <link> tag to the <head> of the index.html file in the root of the project.

For example:

<!-- index.html -->
<!doctype html>
<html lang="en">
  <head>
    <!-- Add a link to your store's CSS file -->
    <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://your-store.com/store.css" />
    ...
  </head>
</html>

Replace https://your-store.com/store.css with the actual URL to your store's main stylesheet. This will allow you to see the correctly styled product cards when running the development server.

Title: Extending tagging with SKUs
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-on-your-website/advanced-implementation/extending-tagging-with-skus
Content: Once included you can review if the SKUs are picked up by using the Nosto Debug Toolbar. If you can see individual SKUs being picked up below the original product details then this is correctly set up.

You can further verify that products are being indexed to the catalog under the Nosto admin by navigating to Tools → Products (https://my.nosto.com/admin/$accountID/campaigns/products/list)

Title: FAQ
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-code-editor/faq
Content: By default, the search indexes all SKUs as a single product. Therefore, even when searching by a specific SKU attribute (like SKU color or ID), the search will return the main product along with all SKUs.

However, because the search returns all SKUs, SKU selection logic can be implemented on the frontend side. This is achieved by checking each SKU to see if it contains text from the search query.

Title: Nosto Service Limits
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/nosto-default-service-limits/nosto-service-limits
Content: Custom Fields
5.000 maximum custom fields across the entire product catalogue
Indexed SKU's (Search)

content.text:
Title: Setting up
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/apis/frontend/implementation-guide-session-api/spa-basics-setting-up
Content: While Nosto crawls sites to replicate the product catalog, it is unable to do so on SPAs. In order to synchronise your product catalog with Nosto, you'll need to leverage the product API to keep the Nosto catalog in sync.

Note: This step must be completed prior to proceeding with the implementation. Without this step, it will be troublesome to preview and debug the recommendations.

Title: Setting up your account
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-on-your-website/manual-implementation/setting-up-your-account
Content: You must use a valid domain for your website. If you are creating a test account and running your store locally, you must use valid TLD as using localhost is not supported.

You cannot use the following domains as they are reserved by the IANA.
.test
.example
.localhost
.invalid
.local
.localdomain
.domain
.lan
.home
.corp
.wip

We recommend using a valid official TLD that is aliased to localhost for testing purposes. You will need to edit your operating-system dependent hosts file to add an alias for the domain you are using.

Nosto periodically crawls your website to keep the catalog data in sync and therefore if you run your webshop locally, Nosto will be unable to crawl your website. In order to overcome this, you will either need to:

make it publicly available using a service such as Pagekite or Ngrok
Use the Products API to keep your catalog in sync

Title: Adding the Customer information
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-on-your-website/manual-implementation/adding-the-customer-information
Content: The customer-reference can be leveraged to unify sessions across channels such as between online and offline. It is a unique identifier provided by you that is used in conjunction with the Nosto cookie. The customer-reference can also be used to uniquely identify users in lieu of an email address.

The customer-reference should be a long, secure and a non-guessable identifier. For example, use your internal customer-id or the customer's loyalty program identifier and use a secure hash function like an HMAC-SHA256 to hash it.

Title: Default Product Tagging
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-on-your-website/manual-implementation/product-tagging/default-product-tagging
Content: The three tag fields, tags1, tags2 and tags3 are simply labels that can be used to annotate tags like discounted, limited collection or other use cases where you might want to filter your Nosto recommendations by certain product groupings.

Custom fields accept a key:value pair where the class of the attribute is the key. Common use cases are material, color or other similar unique identifiers.

Title: Popup Callbacks
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/apis/frontend/js-apis/popups/popup-callbacks
Content: coupon_campaign
String
The identifier of the popup campaign.
coupon_code
String
The discount coupon code given to the customer.
coupon_used
boolean
Whether the coupon was reported as used.

Title: Building your implementation plan
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/quick-start-guide/readme/building-your-implementation-plan
Content: We have prepared dedicated playbooks for advanced setups.

In these cases you might be able to use parts of the Nosto plugins (e.g. for a Shopify headless frontend you can use our app for the data sync but need to implement the frontend components yourself).

We're happy to help you find the ideal approach for your particular tech stack. Please read the matching playbook prior to our conversation:

Headless and SPA (Single Page Application) Frontend: Implementation Methods
Shopify Hydrogen: React Component Library
Magento Hyvä: Built-in support in the Nosto Magento plugin
Custom Platform/Use Case: Product Data Sync GraphQL | REST
Custom Platform/Use Case: Order Data Sync GraphQL
