# Nosto Search Templates — Elie Tahari

> How Nosto search replaces Broadcast's own search on this store, and the constraints that shape it.
> Not a changelog. Template code: `roswell-studios/Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_Nosto`; theme side:
> `Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_2026`.

## The split

Nosto owns the query, facets, sort, pagination, URL state and analytics. **The theme renders every product
card**: a `<nosto-dynamic-card>` fetches `/products/{handle}?section_id=api-nosto-product-card` and injects
the theme's own HTML, so badges, swatches, quick add and prices stay identical to the rest of the site. The
Preact UI around the cards reuses Broadcast's class names, so `theme.css` styles it.

Two card sections exist: `api-nosto-product-card` renders `product-grid-item` for the results grid, and
`api-nosto-product-card-mini` renders `search-product-item` for the header dropdown — matching the two
cards the theme already had. Never reuse `api-product-grid-item`: its `||itemAnimationAnchor||` placeholder
breaks the AOS observer when injected.

## What gates what

**A deployed Nosto template loads on every page regardless of theme settings.** Nosto serves it from the
account and knows nothing about the Shopify theme. The theme setting only controls whether mount points are
rendered — so the code loads either way and simply has nowhere to attach. Confirmed by observation on a
comparable Broadcast store running a deployed template with an unmerged theme.

Consequence: without a live deployment, previewing requires `?nostodebug=true`, a Nosto login and the
Preview toggle. With one, any theme carrying the mounts renders for everyone. That is why the template was
deployed live during development while the live theme stays mount-free.

## Theme-side constraints that are easy to get wrong

- **The mount must sit inside a `[data-products-grid]` wrapper that exists at page load.**
  `card-scroller-window.js` (the iOS memory fix) and `collection-model-switcher.js` both look that wrapper
  up on load and watch it for added cards. Nosto clears the mount on first render, not the wrapper — so the
  wrapper survives and the observers keep working. A bare mount div breaks both.
- **Don't load `collection-filters-form.js` or `collection.js` in Nosto mode.** Their popstate handler
  refetches and replaces `[data-products-grid]`, wiping Nosto's grid.
- **`replaceState`, never `pushState`** for search URL state — see
  `plp-infinite-scroll-and-swatch-fetch.md` for the measured reason.
- Theme custom elements (`quick-add-product`, `hover-images`, `collection-model-switcher`) must be injected
  as parsed HTML, never rendered through JSX — they read their children in the constructor. The Model |
  Product switcher is passed as a `<template>` and cloned.
- Section Rendering has no `section.settings`, so `sizes`, `index: 99` and `card_image_mode` are passed
  explicitly.
- **Header dropdown columns come from the theme's global grid variables** (`snippets/head.liquid`:
  `--COLUMNS` 4, `-MEDIUM` 3, `-SMALL` 2, `-MOBILE` 1); Broadcast's dropdown sets none of its own. The "RS:
  Nosto Settings" column settings write `--COLUMNS*` onto the mount and default to those values, so changing
  them makes the dropdown differ from Broadcast's.
- **Suggestion highlighting:** the theme styles `<mark>` (from Shopify's `styled_text`). Nosto defaults to
  `<strong>`, so the keywords request passes `highlight: { preTag: "<mark>", postTag: "</mark>" }`.

## Translated copy

Elie Tahari ships 6 locales. Nosto's own templates hardcode English, so the theme renders its translated
strings and Shopify sort labels as JSON in `[data-nosto-i18n]` (`snippets/nosto-i18n.liquid`) and the
template reads them. Two traps, both of which pass `shopify theme check`:

1. A literal `{terms}` placeholder inside a `{{ }}` output tag makes Shopify's parser read the closing
   brace as the end of the tag and **reject the file on upload** — the symptom is "Could not find asset"
   for a file that is present and looks fine. Build placeholder strings with `assign` instead.
2. Shopify's `t` filter HTML-escapes translations, so `Search for "{terms}"` arrives as
   `Search for "{terms}"`. Liquid has no unescape filter; the template decodes on read.

## Per-card request volume

Dynamic cards fire one Section Rendering request per card, which runs against the store's standing rule
never to fire a request per product card (see `plp-infinite-scroll-and-swatch-fetch.md`). Measured before
committing to the approach: 5 pages x 36 parallel requests, and a 180-request burst, all returned 200 with
no Cloudflare challenge — including from a flagged datacenter IP. Cards are lazy-loaded. If it ever does
trip, the lever is a batched `/search?q=handle1 OR handle2…&section_id=…` fetch, which returns exact
matches in one request but is slower for first paint.

## Deployment

Two pipelines. The template repo pushes to the **Nosto preview** on every merge to `release/_candidate`;
going live is a deliberate manual step in Nosto Admin (automating it was tried and reverted on the
comparable store). The theme repo deploys `nosto/_candidate` to its own theme. The published Shopify theme
must contain the `api-nosto-*` sections and mounts before a Nosto release goes live, since a Nosto
deployment applies to every theme.

content.text:
**No in-grid editorial-tile field is documented in the Search & Categories API response.** Search results return product hits and related listing data; the docs describe no banner object with a grid position or row/column span. Search merchandising rules affect product results, not editorial-tile layout. See [Use the Search & Categories API](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-api/using-the-search-api) and [Implement Search & Categories](/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search).

For Nosto-managed editorial content, use **Onsite Content Personalization campaigns and placements** separately from the Search API:

* Define a placement in the page’s DOM, or configure a dynamic placement using CSS and URL rules. Request the placement through the Session API; Nosto returns the campaign content for that placement. See [Handling Placements](/techdocs/apis/frontend/implementation-guide-session-api/handling-placements).
* The documented content-campaign response is under `campaigns.content[placementId]`. Its fields include `div_id`, `result_id`, `html`, and `params`. It does **not** document grid coordinates or span values.
* Put the placement where the tile should appear in your grid, then control its column/row span in your Preact/CSS implementation. The docs don’t specify an Nosto Admin setting for configuring tile position or span.

The headless/SPA overview also distinguishes OCP banners returned as HTML from Search/Category listings, which return products and facets: [Headless and SPA (Single Page Application) implementation methods](/techdocs/quick-start-guide/readme/headless-spa-frontend-implementation-methods).

content.text:
Here's the idea. No changes yet.

**Where it happens:** `src/shared/filters/FilterSwatch.tsx`. When a value has no colour or image set in Nosto, it renders the theme's `swatch__button--empty`, which is the grey dashed box. Live does the same for Multicolor, so hiding it is a deliberate change from live. That's fine; I'm just flagging it for the QA table.

**Proposal:** when a value has no `visual`, render no swatch at all, rather than hiding the box with CSS. That leaves no empty element in the markup and needs no new styles.

The one choice is how the text lines up:

```
A. Text shifts left              B. Text stays aligned (blank spacer)
■ Amethyst                       ■ Amethyst
Arabesque Print                    Arabesque Print
Azure Garden                       Azure Garden
■ Black                          ■ Black
```

- **A:** no swatch markup at all for those rows. It's the simplest, but the label text jumps between rows that have a swatch and rows that don't.
- **B:** keep an invisible spacer the size of a swatch (same `swatch__button` box, nothing drawn), so every label in the group starts at the same point.

I'd recommend **B**. With only some colours given swatches in the Admin, A would make the list look ragged.

Facets where no value has a swatch, like Size and Product type, already render no swatch column, so they don't change.

Which do you want, A or B?

content.content:
## Nosto Placements

Placements define **where** on a site a Nosto campaign appears, **how** it loads, and **when** it's shown. Placements are managed under *Experience.AI > Placements*.

### Static vs. Dynamic

- **Static placements** are HTML `div` tags hardcoded into a page template. Each has the `nosto_element` class and a unique identifier, which must match the identifier in the template.
- **Dynamic placements** are injected into the page at load. You define a CSS selector that targets an existing element, then choose how Nosto should insert content relative to it. You don't need to edit templates.

### Configuring Dynamic Placements

1. **Injected element:** A uniquely named `div` that Nosto creates. A descriptive name helps you identify it.
2. **Target via CSS selector:** Any tag, class, or ID on the page can be targeted.
3. **Manipulation method:** Replace, Insert As First, Insert As Last, Before, or After.
4. **Wrapper element:** Simple, Preserve class, Cloned, or No wrapper, for controlling how campaign HTML is injected.
5. **Advanced settings:**
   - *Load only when visible* uses an intersection observer, so content loads when it enters the viewport. This also affects campaign statistics.
   - *Dynamic element detection* uses mutation observers to catch elements that JavaScript adds later, such as mini-cart or mega-menu content.

### Display & Restriction Filters

Dynamic placements can be shown or hidden based on rules:
- **URL filters** and **page type filters**
- **Product filters:** brand, category, tags, product ID, price, availability, and discount status

Manipulation methods control placement and loading. Filters control whether the placement displays at all.

### How Campaigns Attach to Placements

Campaigns, either Onsite Content or Recommendations, are injected into placements when the shopper belongs to a targeted segment and any other conditions are met. The article's segment rules are:

- One placement can serve different campaigns to different segments.
- One placement cannot serve multiple campaigns to the same segment.
- One campaign can use multiple placements for one segment.
- Multiple placements and campaigns can target multiple segments.

### Notes and Limits

- **Conflicts:** If a dynamic placement targets a `div` that also has the `nosto_element` class, the dynamic placement takes precedence and ignores its filters. The Debug Toolbar shows a warning. To fix it, remove the class, retarget the dynamic placement, or change its type to static.
- **Disabled placements** don't show campaigns, though the Debug Toolbar can still reveal them.
- **Testing:** The Preview tool and Nosto Debug Toolbar let you check placement setup on a live URL.
- **Deleting default placements** doesn't remove the placeholder from your template.
- **JavaScript-rendered pages:** The article only covers this through dynamic element detection and visibility-based loading. It doesn't give further guidance on JS-rendered pages, so check the Debug Toolbar when testing those.

content.text:
Noted on the swatch: no change, the empty grey box stays because it's native Broadcast. Here's how Onsite Content Personalization works, and how it could put tiles in the grid. ## How it works **1. Placements: where content can go.** A placement is a named slot on the page, managed in Nosto Admin under *Experience.AI → Placements*. There are two kinds: - **Static:** an empty element in our markup, `
`. Its ID is the placement name. - **Dynamic:** set up entirely in the Admin. A CSS selector targets an existing element, and the Admin chooses where content goes relative to it (replace, before, after, first or last child). It can be limited by URL, page type, or product or category filters, and has an option to detect elements JavaScript adds later. **2. Content campaigns: what goes in a slot.** These are created in the Admin as HTML templates (images, copy, links) and attached to a placement for a **segment** of shoppers. A placement can show different campaigns to different segments, but only one per segment. **3. Fetching and rendering.** The page asks Nosto for its placements, and Nosto returns each one's HTML: ```js api.defaultSession().viewCategory(...).setPlacements(["plp-grid-1", "plp-grid-2"]).load() // → { campaigns: { content: { "plp-grid-1": { div_id, result_id, html, params } } } } ``` The HTML must be inserted through Nosto's `api.placements.injectCampaigns(...)` so clicks are credited to the campaign. A slot with no matching campaign comes back empty. **Two shortcuts already in our repo:** - **`src/elements/Campaign.tsx`**, copied from BaubleBar but never used, wraps Nosto's `` web component. It fetches and injects a placement by itself. - **`src/lib/gridTiles.ts`** already places tiles at numbered slots in the grid. That's the logic we'd reuse. **What none of this does: position or size in the grid.** Nosto has no grid-position or row/column-span setting for content. The search API returns only products, and campaign HTML has no layout fields. So placing a tile and making it span is our code's job. ## How I'd do it for the category grid **1. In Nosto Admin**, which you or Elie Tahari would manage: - **Placements:** a few static placements, e.g. `plp-grid-1`, `plp-grid-2` and `plp-grid-3`. - **Campaigns:** content campaigns attached to them. Each campaign's HTML starts with a wrapper that says where the tile goes and how big it is: ```html
…image, copy, link…
``` **2. In our template:** - **Fetch:** request those placements once per category page load. - **Place:** read the position, columns and rows from each returned campaign and put the tile at that slot using the existing `gridTiles.ts`. - **Size:** make the tile span with CSS grid, `grid-column: span 2; grid-row: span 2`, capped to the columns available at each screen width. - **Inject:** insert the HTML through `injectCampaigns` so clicks are credited to the campaign. - **Empty slots:** a placement with no campaign renders nothing, and the grid closes up. **3. Unchanged:** products still come from Nosto's search API as now. The content is one extra request per page. **Not known yet:** - **Per-collection content:** I don't know whether a campaign on a *static* placement can be limited to one collection. Dynamic placements have category filters; static ones may only target by segment. This decides whether "a different tile on Dresses than on Tops" is possible, so it's worth asking Nosto, or checking in the campaign editor. - **Where the size settings live:** the `data-position`/`data-columns` convention is my proposal. An alternative is campaign parameters, if the editor offers custom fields. I haven't seen the campaign editor. - **Spanning tiles with infinite scroll:** the cap only exists on page 1 on live today. I'd keep tiles to page 1 unless you want otherwise. Should I carry on with this approach? If so, it would help to know how many tile slots you expect per collection and whether the content differs by collection. Sources: - [Nosto: Handling Placements](https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/apis/frontend/implementation-guide-session-api/handling-placements) - [Nosto Help: Placements – General Article](https://help.nosto.com/en/articles/1883767-placements-general-article) - [Nosto: Implement Personalized Campaigns](https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-psn) - [Nosto: Content Personalization](https://www.nosto.com/commerce-experience-platform/content-personalization/)

content.text:
You don't need to know. We can build it so the number of tiles is set entirely in Nosto Admin.

**How:**
- **Naming:** any placement whose name starts with `plp-grid` (e.g. `plp-grid-1`, `plp-grid-spring`) is a grid tile.
- **Discovery:** on each category page, our code asks Nosto which placements exist with `api.placements.getPlacements()`, keeps the `plp-grid…` ones, and requests them all in one call. Nosto's docs say this returns dynamic placements configured in the Admin "regardless of them being rendered", so a new tile slot added in the Admin would show up without a code change. I haven't tested that with a real placement yet.
- **Content:** each returned campaign brings its own position and size in its HTML wrapper, and placements with no campaign for that shopper render nothing.

So it scales from zero to however many tiles there are, without anyone telling us a number. As a safety limit, I'd cap it at something like 6 tiles per page so a misconfigured Admin can't flood the grid. That's easy to change.

**One question still affects the design:** does content need to differ by collection (Dresses vs Tops)? If it does, the tiles will probably need *dynamic* placements, because they can be limited by category and static ones may not. That's also the type the discovery above relies on. If you don't know yet, I'll build for dynamic placements limited by category, since that covers both cases. Nosto can confirm whether static placements can be limited to one collection.

Should I go ahead on that basis? I'd start with the category page itself (the mount, the toolbar and infinite scroll), then add tiles once there's a test placement and campaign in the Admin for me to check against.

I found the relevant Nosto help articles. Here's what they say about creating dynamic placements:

**What dynamic placements are**
- Nosto has two kinds of placements, static and dynamic. Static Placements are Html-based Nosto divs that are hardcoded into a page template. Dynamic Placements are Nosto elements that are dynamically inserted to a page.
- Placement settings are located under *Experience.AI* > *Placements*. There is no limitation to the number of placements you can create.

**How to create one** (from "How to target an element using CSS Selectors?": https://help.nosto.com/en/articles/2341908)
1. **Find the element you want to change.** Right-click it on your site and open the browser inspector to get its tag and class name. In the article's example, it's a div tag with the class name "flexslider".
2. **Create the placement in the Nosto Admin Panel.** Give it a clear name (the example uses "New Banner") and pick the page type, such as Front page. Since the element is not natively present in the page's source code, I change the Placement type to be *Dynamic*.
3. **Configure it.** Give the Placement a unique *ID*, define the *CSS Selector* that points to the element I want to manipulate and choose a *Replace* method.
4. **Turn it on and attach a campaign.** Once the Placement is enabled and an Onsite Content Personalization campaign uses the Placement, the campaign is loaded into the page and replaces the original element.

**Optional controls** (from the general Placements article: https://help.nosto.com/en/articles/1883767)
- Advanced placement settings let you load a placement only when that part of the page scrolls into view.
- Restriction rules and filters let you show or hide a placement based on business rules and page context, such as price range or category.

**For headless or Session API setups** (developer docs)
- Nosto recommends calling `api.placements.getPlacements()`. As long as it is called after the targeted elements have been rendered into the document, it will return both the static and the dynamic CSS and URL rules based placements on the page. Dynamic placements are picked up regardless of them being rendered or not.

The main help article for this is Nosto's "Onsite Content Personalization - General Article" (help.nosto.com/en/articles/1884171). The results only give an overview of how to set up a campaign, not a full step-by-step guide.

**How to create a campaign:**
- You can personalize nearly any part of the store: navigation bars, banners, videos, copy, graphics & logos, and CTAs.
- You can create a new campaign using our built-in wizard. Ready-made templates are available along with an HTML editor, offering full flexibility over design.
- Once a campaign is live and targeting segments, Nosto tracks KPIs. These KPIs are calculated when shoppers are either exposed to the campaign or if they click on it.
- A campaign is loaded onsite using a Nosto Placement, which is a defined element on the page.

**Placements and targeting:**
- Placements define where on the website Nosto campaigns are shown, which can be further manipulated depending on the page's or user's context. If a placement is disabled, it won't show a campaign even when one is bound to it (help.nosto.com/en/articles/1883767).
- By default, if you create a product recommendation slot or an Onsite Content Personalization campaign and do not target a specific segment, it will be displayed to all customers.
- Example use case: the "Visit Custom Event" article shows how to build a campaign under Onsite Content Personalization in the Nosto Admin Panel as a full-screen overlay with two images side by side (articles/2398016).

**Other features (from Nosto's marketing page):**
- Dynamic placements can inject content campaigns anywhere across your store and set visibility conditions based on page type, URL, or product attributes.
- Scheduling: Choose a start and end date for your campaign, or let it run indefinitely.

**Developer docs:** docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-psn covers the technical setup. Placements need to be set up in your store templates. On Shopify and Shopware, you can use our content blocks.

The help center home page (help.nosto.com/en/) has a separate "Onsite Content Personalization (OCP)" section that may have more detailed articles. Several of these articles are 2–8 years old, so the admin screens may look different now.

content.text:
Very little, as long as we keep one thing in mind while building the category page.

**Why it's low risk:** tiles only add to the grid. The category page (mount, toolbar, filters, sort, infinite scroll, cards) doesn't depend on them, and Nosto's tile content comes from a separate request, not the product search. Tiles would plug into one spot: `src/lib/gridTiles.ts`, which already places items at numbered slots among the products, fed today by the theme's `<template>` tiles copied from BaubleBar. Switching that feed to Nosto is new code beside it, not a rewrite.

**What could cause rework, and how I'd avoid it now:**

| Risk | Avoid by |
|---|---|
| Tile placement gets built around the theme `<template>` source | Keep `gridTiles.ts` working from a plain list of `{ position, html }`, so swapping the source to Nosto is just a different list |
| **Spanning tiles break the slot maths.** Today one tile = one slot; a 2×2 tile takes 4 cells, which shifts where products land and how full each infinite-scroll page looks | Don't build anything that assumes one tile = one cell, e.g. no hard-coded "22 products + 2 tiles = 24 cells" |
| **Live's 22-per-page probably leaves room for tiles** (I'm guessing: 24 cells minus 2 one-cell tiles) | Keep page size a setting, as it is now, not a constant |
| Which cards load eagerly or lazily is decided by position in the grid. A large tile near the top changes what's above the fold | Base eager loading on the cell rendered, not the product index, when we add tiles |
| Tiles hidden when filters are applied (BaubleBar's rule, already in our code) | Leave the rule out now. When tiles arrive, it's one setting to decide |

**One thing to raise with Nosto when you contact them:** the SOW lists Onsite Content Personalization as a contracted module. If it isn't enabled on the account, that's Nosto's to switch on, not extra scope. Also ask whether a content campaign can sit in a dynamic placement limited to one category. That's the key question for tiles that differ by collection.

If you're happy to table tiles, I'll build the category page with those guardrails and record the tiles plan in the context doc. Want me to go ahead?

lastPrompt: with regards to eager loading or not, let's assume we can pass a data attribute but i think this can be decided later too, right?

content.text:
Yes, it can wait. Right now every card loads lazily as it scrolls into view (`lazy: true` for all cards in `src/shared/ProductCard.tsx:61`). Nothing loads eagerly based on its position, so there's no position logic for tiles to break.

When we do decide, a data attribute is enough. The theme or the tile can mark how many cells are above the fold (e.g. `data-eager-cells="4"` on the mount), and the grid makes that many rendered cells, products or tiles, load eagerly. It's a change in one place and doesn't affect the category page build.

It's also tied to the performance work. Eager loading the first row would help LCP on PLPs but adds requests up front, so it belongs with the 429 check rather than now.

So I'll table tiles and eager loading and record both in the context doc. Should I go ahead with the category page?

import { useState } from "preact/hooks"
import PaginatedProducts from "@/shared/pagination/PaginatedProducts"
import ProductGrid from "@/shared/ProductGrid"
import { ContentChildrenProps, wrapContent } from "@/shared/ContentWrapper"
import NoResults from "@/shared/NoResults"
import Toolbar from "@/shared/toolbar/Toolbar"
import { getEditorialTiles } from "@/lib/themeSettings"

/**
 * Collection page layout mirrors sections/collection.liquid: collection nav (same as search), then the products
 * grid with any editorial tiles.
 */
function PlpPage({ foundProducts, loading }: ContentChildrenProps) {
  const [tiles] = useState(getEditorialTiles)

  if (!foundProducts && !loading) return <NoResults />
  return (
    <>
      <Toolbar />
      <ProductGrid loading={loading}>
        <PaginatedProducts tiles={tiles} />
      </ProductGrid>
    </>
  )
}

export default wrapContent("category", PlpPage)

# Elie Tahari — Reference Brand Library
> 13 confirmed North Star brands. Source: CLIENT_CONTEXT §5 + call history (Mar 19 + Mar 26 + Apr 2 calls).
> Owner: Tom Wittlin (Designer) / Yoshitha (MP) | Updated: 2026-05-20
> Status: ✅ Confirmed by Jeremey Tahari across multiple design review calls.

---

## The 13 North Stars

| Brand | What to steal | Jeremy's exact words / context | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Loewe** | Mobile bottom nav (sticky, app-native feel), subtle color-on-scroll, color blocking on sign-in, UX restraint, type discipline | *"I'm a big fan of the Loewe site."* — Jeremey, Mar 26. *"It's very native to mobile UX with nav bars being at the bottom."* | Mar 19, Mar 26 |
| **Hermès** | Desktop horizontal-scroll PDP, Apple Pay scan-from-desktop, checkout flow | *"Has been buying via Hermès Apple Pay scan-from-desktop."* — Rob (Chief of Staff) | Mar 19, Apr 2 |
| **Saint Laurent** | Minimal type sizing throughout — every font is smaller than you'd expect | Confirmed North Star in call notes — minimal typography hierarchy | Mar 19 |
| **Dior** | Assertive cookie banner | Referenced as having the right cookie UX | Mar 19 |
| **JW Anderson** | Edgy creative direction — **but UX is too obscure** (cautionary tale, not pure North Star) | Call notes: *"edgy, but UX is too obscure"* — not a verbatim Jeremey quote | Mar 19 |
| **Cara Cara** | Collection page storytelling — delivery drop narrative, campaign image + description linking to drop collection | Tom's prior client. Referenced for PDP collection storytelling direction. | Apr 1, May 4 |
| **Phoebe Philo** | Minimal — admired, but too far as North Star | Call notes: *"too minimal as North Star but admired"* — not confirmed as verbatim quote | Mar 19 |
| **Tory Burch** | PLP subcategory chips (bigger, underlined, in bronze), footer T&Cs placement at bottom (small + gray) | Call notes: subcategory chips styled like Tory Burch — bigger, underlined, in bronze (Apr 2) | Mar 12, Apr 2 |
| **Cult Gaia** | Cookie banner: Accept + X (policy) — clean binary, no dark patterns | *"Gaia had a really good one that Jeremy loved."* — Claudia, Apr 1 | Apr 1 |
| **COS** | Mobile UX — dynamic auto-play videos | Referenced for mobile UX inspiration, auto-play content | Mar 12, Mar 19 |
| **TWP (The White Pep / The Wardrobe Project)** | Peer-set positioning — contemporary luxury womenswear | Peer comp referenced in brand positioning calls | Mar 12, Mar 19 |
| **Khaite** | Slim swatches reference (small, underline-style not box-style) | Referenced for swatch style direction | Apr 2 |
| **Ralph Lauren** | CTA underline placement on hover, sub-line strategy (multi-label handling) | *"Like Ralph Lauren's CTA placement"* — Jeremey | Mar 26, Apr 2 |

---

## Competitive Peer Set (not North Stars — brands they compete with)

| Brand | Relationship |

04-engineering/tech-context.md:24:- **Nosto account:** `shopify-35089973385` (Shopify Markets: the storefront loads Nosto through the market-aware app proxy, `/apps/proxy/script/shopify/market/nosto.js?merchant=shopify-35089973385&market=…`).
04-engineering/tech-context.md:25:- **Account provisioned 2026-10-22.** Search, Search Templates and Category Merchandising are all enabled (`searchEnabled`, `searchTemplatesEnabled`, `categoriesEnabled` true; `searchApiUrl` `https://search.nosto.com/api/`). Was unprovisioned and 403ing from 2026-10-05 until Nosto acted. **Still open: multi-currency is USD-only** on a Shopify Markets store with the market-aware embed.

You're right that it should work that way, and it does: the browser never downloads that 2000px file. It's only the fallback `src` on the hidden hover image, and live hadn't loaded it at all. The browser picks from the `srcset` list (136w up to 1950w) by multiplying the `sizes` width by the screen's pixel density. That's the 2x rule you describe: on a Retina screen it chose the 640px file for the card.

**I can't reproduce the blur yet.** At 1x and 2x, before and after moving the slider, our cards load exactly the same files as live. The 2x screenshots of the first card look equally sharp on both. Both are at `/Users/pk/Documents/roswell-studios/Elie_Tahari_TAHARI_Nosto/.playwright-mcp/qa/`, named `live-plp-card-slide2-2x.png` and `dev-plp-card-slide2-2x.png`.

**I did find a related issue, on both live and ours:** `sizes` underestimates the card. The theme's formula, `calc((100vw - 100px) / 4 - 32px)`, gives 303px at 1440, but the card actually renders at 347px; the formula assumes 32px gaps where the grid uses 4px. So the browser picks one size smaller than ideal: 320px at 1x for a 347px card, and 640px at 2x where 694px is needed. That's slightly soft on both themes, so it doesn't explain ours looking worse than live. Correcting the formula would sharpen both, but it's Broadcast's card snippet, so it would change the live theme too.

The filter fixes you approved are all done, checked against live on your dev theme, and pushed. The acceptance criteria file is ticked to match.

**Price filter** (`f71c4b4` in the Nosto repo, `4433de0` in the theme). It now matches live:
- **Layout:** the slider starts at $0 and ends at the highest price in the results. "$" From / To inputs sit underneath, with no value labels. Track, dots, inputs, "$", the "-" spacer and the "From" / "To" labels sit in the same positions as live.
- **Inputs:** empty with placeholders until a range is set. They fill as you drag, and typing a value and pressing Enter applies it.
- **Translations:** labels and currency come from the theme ("From", "To", the cart currency symbol).
- **Bug found while checking:** Nosto reports the results' own min and max even when no price filter is set, which made it look filtered from the start. Fixed, and covered by a new unit test.

**Earlier fixes**, in the Nosto repo:
- `58ee644`: "$" on price values and price chips.
- `f38506d`: no count on the toolbar Filters button.
- `f1f4164`: chip and "More options" line height, now 25.1px chips as on live.

**Acceptance criteria file:** Filters #6, #7 and #8 are ✅. The Price criterion now reads "$0 to the highest price in the current results", since live doesn't round.

All 205 unit tests pass, along with typecheck and lint.

Next in the order:
1. Finish the collection page comparison: mobile and tablet, infinite scroll, and filters on a collection.
2. The grid and card loading states against live, on both search and collections.

content.text:
The toolbar loads in my browser on your dev theme. `debugtoolbar.min.js` comes from `connect.nosto.com`, the toolbar element is on the page, and the theme is still `158466539657` ("Development (bd46cb-PKs-Macbook-Pro)"). So the problem is probably in your browser. I can't see your browser, so these are the likely causes, most likely first:

1. **The toolbar was closed or hidden earlier.** It has minimise (–) and close (×) buttons, and the bottom bar has "Hide bar". It remembers that choice for the site, so `?nostodebug=true` loads it but keeps it hidden. Check: open a **private window**, log in to Nosto there, and load the same URL. If it shows, clear the site data for elietahari.com in your normal browser.
2. **An ad or tracking blocker** is blocking `connect.nosto.com`. Check: in DevTools → Network, filter for `debugtoolbar`. If it's blocked or missing, pause the blocker for the site.
3. **The URL lost the parameter.** Shopify sometimes redirects and drops query parameters, especially `/` → `/?…` or a market redirect. Check that the address bar still shows `nostodebug=true` once the page has loaded.

Quick test for which one it is: in the DevTools console on that page, run

```js
document.querySelector('nostodebug-bar')
```

If it returns an element, the toolbar loaded and is hidden (cause 1). If it returns `null`, the script didn't load (cause 2 or 3).

input.description: Research Shopify category colour metafield
input.prompt:
Research question (web research only; do not edit any files or touch any repo):

A Shopify Plus fashion store (Elie Tahari) uses Shopify's Standard Product Taxonomy category metafield for colour — `shopify.color-pattern` (a list of metaobject references to `shopify--color-pattern` entries, each linked to a taxonomy base colour like Black, Blue, Beige, with a swatch hex/image). Their live storefront filter (Shopify Search & Discovery) uses it, so swatches come from Shopify.

They are moving onsite search/filtering to Nosto, which cannot index metaobject references usefully (it stores the raw `gid://shopify/Metaobject/...` IDs). Plan: add a plain-text metafield (e.g. `custom.color_family`) populated by a Shopify Flow from the category colour, and facet on that in Nosto.

The question: **is there value in continuing to keep the Shopify category colour metafield (`shopify.color-pattern`) populated and accurate, even after Nosto stops using it?** Find out concretely what else in Shopify and beyond consumes the Standard Product Taxonomy category + category metafields, especially color-pattern. Areas to check:
- Shopify Search & Discovery filters (native storefront filters) and Shopify's own storefront search relevance.
- Google Shopping / Google & YouTube channel / Merchant Center feeds (google_product_category, color attribute), Meta/Facebook & Instagram catalogs, TikTok, Pinterest, Microsoft — do they pull category metafields or taxonomy?
- Shop app / Shop Pay / Shopify Catalog / "agentic commerce" (AI shopping agents, Shopify Catalog API / UCP, ChatGPT/Perplexity shopping integrations) — do they use taxonomy attributes?
- SEO: structured data (Product schema `color`), whether Shopify themes or Shopify output category attributes into JSON-LD; any SEO effect.
- Shopify Markets / translation, Shopify Collective, B2B, POS, analytics/reporting by category attributes.
- Shopify Flow: confirm whether Flow can read a metaobject reference metafield's referenced entry fields (e.g. the color-pattern entry's label/taxonomy value) and write a text metafield — and any known limits (list references, bulk backfill of existing products).
- Any downsides of letting it go stale.

Use current official sources first (shopify.dev, help.shopify.com, Shopify changelog, Google Merchant Center help, Meta commerce docs); note dates. Distinguish verified facts (with source URL) from inference, and say plainly when you couldn't confirm something.

Return a concise report (aim for under ~600 words): a short verdict, then a bullet list of concrete consumers/benefits each with a source link and confidence (confirmed / likely / unconfirmed), then the Flow feasibility notes, then any risks of letting it go stale.
