Title: Implementing Search page
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/implement-search-using-code-editor/implementing-search-page
Content: When serpPathRedirect parameter is set to true, the application after search submission will redirect the browser to the search page specified in serpPath. Default behavior will only rewrite browser history to the specified path, without reloading the page.

In many cases, the search/autocomplete input is located on a different page from the search results. For example, on the landing or home page; or it may be always visible in the store's header. For those cases, it may be desired to redirect the user to the search results when a search request is submitted. If search page redirect is not configured, Nosto integration assumes that the search results should be rendered on the current page.

The redirect is controlled by two configuration variables:

serpPath (string) - specifies the path to the search page (follows the browser's location.pathname).
serpPathRedirect - (boolean or function) - combined variable that controls whether or not the redirect is enabled, and also provides a custom navigation mechanism if necessary.

When serpPathRedirect is omitted or set to false, the default behaviour is to update the browser's history (i.e. rewrite the current URL) to add the search query parameter.

When serpPathRedirect is set to true, the browser will redirect to the search page indicated by serpPath upon search submission. The default mechanism is location.href = {targetUrl} . If the current page already matches the search path, the search query parameter will be added instead.

When serpPathRedirect is set to a function, it will be called instead of setting location.href . This is useful to, for example, interact with your frontend framework, inject custom logic before redirect or handle special cases for redirect. For example:

init({
    serpPath: '/search',
    serpPathRedirect: (query: SearchQuery, options: AutocompleteOptions | undefined) => {
        location.href = `https://store.com/search/${query?.query}` // Query as a path param
    },
})

In function form, serpPathRedirect exposes the main query object that holds the data which would instead be send to Nosto. The second object simply holds information about the click.

export interface AutocompleteOptions {
    isKeyword?: boolean // true if the user clicked on a suggested keyword
}

Checkout our API documentation on serpPathRedirect

Title: Search page redirects
Link: https://docs.nosto.com/techdocs/implementing-nosto/implement-search/using-search-templates-starter/customizations/search-page-redirects
Content: If the user performs a search from any page that is not the SERP (e.g., the homepage, a content page), the application will perform a full-page redirect to the SERP.

The browser is redirected to /search?q=<your-query>.
The SERP then loads, reads the q parameter from the URL, and automatically fetches and displays the results for that query.

This ensures a consistent experience, where a search always leads the user to the dedicated, fully-featured search results page.

content.text:
I added your to-do as queue item 17: on a collection that has no products and no filters applied, hide the Reset button, and show it only when filters are active. It's committed (dde4fab).

**Do Nosto's docs say how to check for double page views?** Not for our setup. You're right that I assumed too much. Here's what they actually say:

- **For their Session API only** ("Leveraging Features", plus the custom-implementation page "Implement Personalized Campaigns"): calling `load()` increments the page view counter (`pv` in the `ev1` response). Any later request on the same page should use `update()` or `load({skipPageViews: true})`. For QA, they point to the debug toolbar's **Visitor** tab and the `ev1` request in the network tab.
- **For `createRecommendationRequest`** (what the carousel component uses): nothing. No page says whether its `load()` counts a page view, and none explains how to check for double counting. Nosto's docs assistant says the same thing: the `load()`/`update()` rule is only documented for the Session API and shouldn't be applied to `createRecommendationRequest` without checking.

**Where my claim was weak:**
- I only looked at the `ev1` requests and ignored the other Nosto requests on the page.
- Seeing the same `pv` in both responses only shows the counter didn't go up. It doesn't prove Nosto's reporting didn't record a second view, and nothing in the docs says it would show up there.

So "it doesn't look like page views are double counted" is my inference, not something the docs back up. I suggest this wording for the Autoloading bullet instead:

> *Autoloading:* your autoloader is still on, and `<nosto-section-campaign>` makes its own recommendation request, so each page with a carousel sends two `ev1` requests. The docs say to disable autoloading when requesting campaigns yourself, and the page-view guidance (`update()` / `skipPageViews`) only covers the Session API. Can you confirm whether the component's request counts as an extra page view, and whether autoloading should be turned off?

Want me to put that into the Slack draft? I can also list every Nosto request on a dev page load, not just `ev1`, so we can include what actually goes out.

content.text:
Good catch. That's the flag the docs describe, and it settles most of the question.

- **What the docs say:** later requests on the same page should be sent with `skipPageViews: true` so they don't count as another page view. Until now I'd only seen that guidance for the Session API.
- **What your request shows:** one of the two `ev1` requests carries `skipPageViews=true`, so it isn't counted as a page view.
- **Which request it is:** it's almost certainly the carousel's own request. It has `response_mode: JSON_ORIGINAL`, which matches the JSON request the carousel component (`<nosto-section-campaign>`) makes.
- **Who sets the flag:** not the component. In `node_modules/@nosto/web-components/dist/main.cjs.js:608` it calls plain `load()` with no flags. Nosto's own script must add `skipPageViews` because a page view was already recorded for the page.

One thing to confirm, to avoid another assumption: the other `ev1` request (the autoloader's) should **not** have `skipPageViews`. If it doesn't, the page counts exactly one view and there's no double counting.

If that holds, I'd simplify the Autoloading bullet in the Slack draft to:

> *Autoloading:* your autoloader is still on, and `<nosto-section-campaign>` makes its own recommendation request, so pages with a carousel send two `ev1` requests. The second one is sent with `skipPageViews=true`, so page views aren't double counted. Can you confirm autoloading should stay on, since the docs suggest disabling it when requesting campaigns yourself?

Want me to update the draft with that?

Something else I noticed in the same file: the other Nosto component, `<nosto-campaign>`, has a built-in `lazy` option that waits until it scrolls into view before loading (line 637). `<nosto-section-campaign>`, the one we use, doesn't. So our own deferral in `rs-nosto-carousel.js` is still needed.

Message 1 of 4

@Justin O'Hara @Lotta Järvinen

Quick progress update on Tahari, with a few questions in separate messages below so we can keep each one in its own thread.

 

Rendering through Nosto, matching the live theme (on our dev theme): autocomplete, search results page, category pages and recommendation carousels.

 

Still in progress:

  • UI and performance refinements: loading states, avoiding layout shift while results and carousels load, etc.

 

  • Reworking the colour filter and swatches, since the current setup isn't compatible with Nosto.

 

Next: recommendation carousel placements and editorial tiles in the category grid.

Message 2 of 4

1. Please enable Content Personalization

Content Experience Cloud → Content Personalization shows a Contact us screen. Could you enable it, and confirm:

  • Can a content campaign use a dynamic placement limited to one category, so each collection can have its own tiles?

 

  • What's the recommended way to pass a tile's grid position and size (how many columns and rows it spans) to the template? Our plan is data attributes on the campaign HTML, read by the template, which also handles the layout. Is there a better or built-in option?
Message 3 of 4

2. Recommendation carousels

We have carousel rendering working with <nosto-section-campaign placement="…" section="…"> (JSON response, our own Shopify section with the theme's carousel and product card), but only with the Nosto multi-currency app embed turned off.

  • Multi-currency: all our product cards (search, category pages and carousels) render through dynamic product cards, so Shopify renders each card in the shopper's market and the price shows in the market's currency.
